sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
A **Bode plot** graphs \(|H|\) in decibels and \(\angle H\) in degrees against frequency on a log axis. Logs turn the products in a factored transfer function into sums, so you can draw each pole and zero as a simple straight-line piece and add them up.

Each real pole bends the magnitude down by \(-20\) dB/decade after its corner and contributes up to \(-90^\circ\) of phase. Each real zero bends it up by \(+20\) dB/decade and contributes up to \(+90^\circ\). The phase of each factor changes over roughly a decade below to a decade above the corner, and is half-way (\(\pm45^\circ\)) at the corner. The true curve is 3 dB off the asymptote at a single corner.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ |H|_{dB} = 20\log_{10}|H| \]
\[ H(j\omega) = K\,\frac{1 + j\omega/\omega_z}{(1 + j\omega/\omega_{p1})(1 + j\omega/\omega_{p2})} \]
Single pole: slope \(-20\) dB/dec above \(\omega_p\), phase \(-45^\circ\) at \(\omega_p\), \(-90^\circ\) far above.
A pole at the origin, \(1/(j\omega)\): \(-20\) dB/dec everywhere with a constant \(-90^\circ\).
sections.figure_alt: Double-pole Bode magnitude: the asymptote has a corner at omega_p while the exact dashed curve sits below it.

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
Sketch \(H = \dfrac{100}{(1 + j\omega/10^3)(1 + j\omega/10^5)}\).

- Below \(10^3\): flat at \(20\log 100 = 40\) dB.
- From \(10^3\) to \(10^5\): falls at \(-20\) dB/dec, losing 40 dB, so 0 dB at \(10^5\).
- Above \(10^5\): \(-40\) dB/dec.

Phase: \(0^\circ\) at low frequency, about \(-90^\circ\) between the poles (around \(10^4\)), heading to \(-180^\circ\) far above \(10^5\).

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Using \(10\log\) instead of \(20\log\) for voltage gain.
- Starting the slope change a decade early: magnitude bends **at** the corner; it is the phase that starts a decade before.
- Forgetting that a factor of 10 in gain is 20 dB, and 2× is about 6 dB.
- Ignoring the DC gain \(K\) when placing the flat line.

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: Bode plots are the main tool for the feedback chapters. Gain-bandwidth, closed-loop bandwidth and phase margin are all read off sketches like these, so practise drawing the asymptotes quickly and checking the phase a decade on either side of each corner.
